newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends firm in lack lustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends firm in lack lustre trade.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed higher against the dollar on Monday due to a lack of demand for the greenback, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.72 to the dollar, after opening at 58.78 and rising to 58.70, they said. The rupee closed at 58.80 on Thursday, the last trading day.
"There was no commercial demand for dollars, but some banks just quoted two-way prices," said an American Express bank dealer.
The Central Bank fixed buying and selling prices at 58.6179 and 59.8021.
"The dollar-rupee exchange rate should be ranged this week unless there is a big import bill, because most (banks) are either squared or carrying plus positions," said a Deutsche Bank dealer.
Overnight call money closed at 9.5 percent after opening at 8.75, dealers said.
Supply was restricted since a number of banks who lend money on the call market regularly, had invested in the Central Bank repo at 8.5 percent, dealers said.
